fair_value_reason: Mean of the five revised fair values ($225, $230, $229, $230, $229 = $228.6), rounded. The inputs are now consistent and match the primary documents: net debt ~$22.9B ($22.8B at 6/30/26 per the 10-Q), ~393-394M diluted shares, 2027 EBITDA ~$8.72-8.75B (below the unaffirmed target floor), NTM EPS ~$9.5-9.6 at 23.5-24x, 12.3-12.5x NTM EBITDA and a 4.6-4.75% FCF yield. No agent error remains to correct.
supervisor_summary: In round 2 every forecaster took up the round-1 corrections: the 2027 targets are unaffirmed, net debt is $22.8B, ~393M shares, current multiples, and the Fed hiking cycle. They now cluster at a $225-230 fair value with a ~59% chance WM closes above today's $207 in a year (median ~$215, +4%, plus a ~1.8% dividend). I re-checked the one volatile input (FOMC odds, unchanged at 44% October / 74% December) and found nothing that justifies moving off the mean, so the ladder, fair value ($229) and thesis break ($178) are the forecaster consensus. The narrow spread partly reflects herding on round-1 feedback, so treat it as a steady low-vol compounder with a modest edge. The main risks are the Feb-2027 first guide under a new CEO and the rate path.
key_drivers: The first formal 2027 guide comes with Q4-2026 results (late Jan/Feb 2027) under new CEO Morris. The June-2025 targets ($8.85-9.15B EBITDA) are 'not reissued or affirmed' (Q4-2025 8-K note h). All five agents now model ~$8.72-8.75B.

Price over cost: core price is 5.7% vs ~3-4% cost inflation, and FY26 EBITDA ($8.15-8.25B) and FCF ($3.75-3.85B) guidance was held despite a ~1% volume decline. Peers (RSG, WCN, GFL, Casella) show the same pattern.
Multiple: ~22.7x FY27 EPS vs RSG ~27.5x, with the Fed in a hiking cycle (Oct hike 44%, Dec 74% on prediction markets). That caps a re-rating and keeps the right tail thin.
Capital return: ~$2B/yr of buybacks, a $3.78 dividend and leverage of 2.96x guided lower, giving ~393M diluted shares and ~$22.9B net debt at the horizon.
Q3 print on Oct-27: H2 volume flat or not, and whether FY26 guidance is reaffirmed.
